expectations.text: The artifact is a durable policy or rules document, not a one-time access guide.
expectations.evidence: The response is structured as a Production Access policy with a policy statement, purpose, scope, normative requirements, exceptions, compliance/reporting, owner, effective date, and revision sections.

expectations.text: Scope, covered roles, owner, and effective date are explicit.
expectations.evidence: The scope section covers all engineers and production access, identifies on-call engineer and incident commander as requesters, and states the effective date as 2026-10-01; the owner is explicitly Platform Security.

expectations.text: Required, permitted, and prohibited behavior use consistent normative language.
expectations.evidence: The policy consistently uses required/prohibitive language such as 해야 한다, 필요하다, 금지, 허용하지 않는다, and 해서는 안 된다 for approvals, logging, duration, permitted purpose, and prohibited conduct.

expectations.text: The SEV-1 exception, approving authority, and 24-hour review are explicit.
expectations.evidence: The SEV-1 section explicitly permits the incident commander to approve urgent access when manager approval cannot wait, limits it to the minimum scope/time, requires security-team logging, and requires post-review within 24 hours.

expectations.text: Reporting and violation handling are discoverable without reading a procedure.
expectations.evidence: The dedicated 준수, 보고 및 조치 section states that discovered or suspected violations must be reported promptly to the security team and that the security team reviews violations and access records and coordinates follow-up.
